area.title: Review page (check your answers)
area.scope: The review (check your answers) page in every variant: journey, draft, submitted read-only and action-required views, its sections, cards, rows, change links, incomplete-card errors and header (status, dates, import reference numbers); and what counts as complete enough to submit. Stops at the declaration and submitted pages (declaration-and-submitted) and at the amend, cancel-amend, copy and delete actions the header offers (manage-notifications). Includes the high-risk plants frontend check answers page and its review helpers and lateness rules.

sources.role: the answers to the two notification view header questions the 25 November re-distil raised from ruling:sam-2026-11-19 point 2. It settles c-438: once the amend confirmation page exists, 'Amend this notification' on the header is a link to that page rather than a posting button, because the first click then changes nothing, a POST that only renders a page is the wrong verb and leaves a re-POST on the back button without JavaScript, and Delete already opens its confirmation page by href in the same header; Copy as new keeps its own form because it still changes something, Delete stays a link, and no action shares another's form, in live animals, germinal products and plants alike. Point 2 of the 19 November ruling is unweakened, its subject being that no action shares another action's form, which a link does not do. It settles c-447 the other way from the default: the plants header gains a Copy as new action so both journeys offer the same three actions. That is wiring rather than a feature build, because every layer beneath it is already on main - the plants backend serves POST /{referenceNumber}/copy with a NotificationCopyMapper, the plants frontend's real and stub persistence both implement copy, and its engine holds copyJourney - and only the header's copyAction and route are missing. The plants backend therefore needs nothing and trade-imports-plants-backend does not join this programme's repos; inc-123 takes plantsfrontend alongside backend, frontend and tests, and inc-124's stale-copy return takes plants too. Plants' copy carries plants' own answers, so the carried-over-trade against cleared-shipment split is read against plants' own fields rather than copied field for field.

sources.role: the decision that pagination is kept everywhere and that its earlier removal was an error: every address book list and every address picker pages, and no requirement says a list of an organisation's addresses is served or shown unpaginated. It drops req-611's 'unpaginated' clause and supersedes ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6 on that point alone, because that point's reasoning rested on the address book's list endpoint taking no role and so having to be read whole and paged for display, which is no longer true of the service: RequestedListFilters takes roles and searchRoles, AddressController lists one page at a time with page and pageSize, and ListPaging sets 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, exactly the bounds ruling:paul-2026-11-05 point 8 names. The role filter runs in the service before the page is cut, so paging the API cannot make it wrong, and Paul's point 8 stands in full. The rest of ruling:ian-2026-11-23 stands: the pickers page at eight, the one-page clause of inc-087's criteria 7, 8 and 9 stays dropped with req-594 and req-595, and the 'Selected address' restatement comes back with the paging. EUDPA-827 is the fix and has landed on the animals frontend's main. It settles conflict c-292 by keeping the plants contact picker's pagination and inset, and the contact picker pages at eight rather than five, confirmed by Ian the same day, so every picker in both journeys pages at the figure the INS address book list already uses and ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 1 set for the other pickers.

sources.role: the decision on transporter management, outranking ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm on that point and lifting claim c-285: the address book manages transporters as per-organisation records, and adding one mid journey uses the address book hand-off already built for addresses (inc-077, inc-078, inc-080). A transporter is its own record in its own transporters collection inside the address book service, not the Address model; it has no roles and stores a private-or-commercial type instead; a commercial transporter country is forced to XI (Northern Ireland) with no reference-data lookup, while a private transporter keeps its choice of export country. Approved transporters are parked.

claims.statement: This ruling settles whether the service manages transporters at all and, if so, whether the address book or something else does - the question ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm point 5 (claim c-285) left blocked pending requirements.
claims.quote: On transporter management, which Sam's ruling of 9 October (afternoon) left blocked pending requirements — whether the service manages transporters at all and, if so, whether the address book or something else does (`ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm` point 5, claim c-285):
claims.note: answers the block ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm point 5 left, recorded there as claim c-285

claims.statement: The address book manages transporters, which are saved per organisation just like other addresses.
claims.quote: My decision is that the address book will manage the transporters, just like other addresses which are saved per organisation.

claims.statement: Adding a transporter uses the same pattern of moving to the address book mid journey that adding other addresses uses.
claims.quote: It will use the same pattern with moving to the address book mid journey, like other addresses when adding transporters - it's essentially the same pattern.

claims.statement: The earlier block rested on the concept of 'approved transporters': a list that may be managed in MDM for all organisations and added to each organisation's own transporter options.
claims.quote: I think that previous ruling was based on the concept of 'approved transporters' which may be a list managed in MDM for all organisations that will be added to the organisations individual transporter options.

claims.statement: Approved transporters are not to be worried about for now.

sources.role: the decision on what the address book stores for an address's type and uses (EUDPA-711): "use" is renamed "role" everywhere, in the record, the API, the code, the copy keys, the tests and the spec, and an address holds the roles it can play on a notification, being place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer, place of destination and branch address. The address book stores roles only and requires at least one; it does not store an address type and ignores one a client sends, the address type being the INS front door's grouping of roles worked out from them. The grouping of roles into sending, receiving and branch is the address book's internal rule rather than part of its API, and it refuses roles from more than one group, and a consignee, importer or place of destination outside the United Kingdom. The list takes role, repeatable and any-of, and searchRole, in place of addressType, use and searchUse. A role a new notification type needs is added in code, each role in exactly one group. Addresses saved before the change are not migrated: after release the addresses collection is dropped in dev and test with CDP tooling and the address book restarted, and locally the stack is restarted. The address book's list and every address picker keep pagination even though the Design Release 2.1 prototype has none, the list API paging with page and pageSize of 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, because organisations in test environments hold thousands of addresses; no requirement to list an organisation's addresses unpaginated is built, which ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6 later reads the other way for req-611 and so outranks on that point alone.

sources.role: the owner's decisions: outranks every other source. Search boxes use the real frontend's accessible component with MDM's entries. JavaScript behaviour follows the toolbox rule with graceful degradation; JavaScript-only prototype behaviour, pop-ups included, waits on design in its own theme. Commodity catalogue and search wait on MDM; transporter management waits on requirements; the INS dashboard's summary information waits on its requirements. The overview, review, declaration and confirmation are set-owned, and shared parts change add-only. Where plants has the same page or behaviour, the same increment changes it. Each notification list is reframed in its own frontend. The report groups work as ready or blocked. Claims marked as the orchestrator's apply Sam's principles and are not his rulings; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates covers templates and the dashboard narrowing.

claims.statement: Sam rules that, as a pre-step for these increments, three questions are answered: is it possible with off-the-shelf GDS; if not, with other complementary off-the-shelf components; if not, why is the atypical thing strongly required. claims.statement: Increments are grouped into themes, and the themes are drawn from the evidence.
claims.quote: Themes: group the increments into themes based on the evidence.

claims.statement: Each theme's boundary is set by the code it touches.
claims.quote: Draw the boundaries by the code each one touches
claims.note: New.

claims.quote: so themes can be built in parallel on separate machines without conflicting PRs.

claims.statement: The ruling's DR1 paragraph has an elision marked [...]: what the omitted words said about the DR1 parity backlog is not recorded.
The ruling does not say what makes a difference 'truly exceptional', so when a question for people is warranted is left open.

The ruling limits DR1 use to clashes between 'the real frontend' and the prototype; it does not say which frontend that is, or whether DR1 judgements apply to differences in the INS frontend, the backends or other repos.
The ruling does not say which override wins when a DR1 judgement and a real constraint the prototype cannot express point different ways on the same difference.
The ruling does not say what a real service does where a real constraint overrides the prototype: whether it keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as the constraint allows.
The ruling does not say whether a feature or behaviour a real service has that Design Release 2.1 does not show at all counts as a difference to remove, or is left alone.
The ruling does not say what to do where the code two themes need to touch overlaps, so no boundary keeps their pull requests from conflicting.

claims.statement: Uploading documents is optional: Save and continue, or Save and return to overview, with every document field left empty moves on without any error.

sources.role: how the real animals frontend renders today

claims.statement: The review page lives at /notifications/<reference>/notification-view under the live-animals service and is headed 'Review your notification'.
claims.quote: Review your notification

claims.statement: The review page's browser title is 'Review your notification - Import notification service - GOV.UK' when the notification is complete.
claims.quote: Review your notification - Import notification service - GOV.UK

claims.statement: When the notification is unfinished, the review page's browser title is prefixed 'Error: ', on the first GET as well as after a refused Continue.
claims.quote: Error: Review your notification - Import notification service - GOV.UK

claims.statement: Above the heading, the review shows a journey strip with a status tag and the notification reference in bold; a draft shows a blue 'Draft' tag.
claims.quote: Draft GBN-AG-26-QHN0C4

claims.statement: A submitted notification's review shows a green 'Submitted' tag in the journey strip in place of Draft.
claims.quote: Submitted GBN-AG-26-QQ1X0N

claims.statement: The review is laid out as six numbered level-2 sections in this order: '1. About the consignment', '2. Description of the goods', '3. Transport and arrival', '4. Documents', '5. Consignment parties', '6. Contact address'.
claims.quote: 1. About the consignment | 2. Description of the goods | 3. Transport and arrival | 4. Documents | 5. Consignment parties | 6. Contact address

claims.statement: The six sections carry anchor ids: about-the-consignment, description-of-the-goods, transport-and-arrival, documents-section, consignment-parties and contact-address-section.
claims.quote: <H2 class="govuk-heading-m" id="documents-section">4. Documents

claims.statement: A visible section break (govuk-section-break--l --visible) separates each numbered section from the next.
claims.quote: <HR class="govuk-section-break govuk-section-break--l govuk-section-break--visible">

claims.statement: Every card on the review sits under its own level-3 subsection heading; on a new notification the subsection headings are, in order: 'Where is this consignment coming from?', 'Main reason for import', 'Additional details', 'Arrival details', 'Transport details', 'Upload documents', 'Roles and addresses', 'Contact address for this consignment'.
claims.quote: Where is this consignment coming from? | Main reason for import | Additional details | Arrival details | Transport details | Upload documents | Roles and addresses | Contact address for this consignment

claims.statement: Card titles are level-4 headings, one per summary card, so the number of level-4 headings equals the number of cards.
claims.quote: <H4 class="govuk-summary-card__title">

claims.statement: A brand-new notification's review shows eight cards: Import details, Reason for import, Additional animal details, Arrival details, Transport details, Uploaded documents, Roles and addresses, and Contact address for this consignment.
claims.ref: trace 71d37 actions call@837 to call@857; trace 11c41 action call@663
claims.quote: Import details | Reason for import | Additional animal details | Arrival details | Transport details | Uploaded documents | Roles and addresses | Contact address for this consignment

claims.statement: With no commodity line, section 2 shows no 'Commodity details' subsection or commodity card at all; only 'Additional details' stands.
claims.quote: 2. Description of the goods / Additional details / Additional animal details

claims.statement: Once a commodity line exists, section 2 shows a 'Commodity details' subsection with one card per line, titled '<common name> (<commodity code>) — <species>'.
claims.quote: Cow (0102) — Bos taurus

claims.statement: The commodity card lists Commodity code, Common name, Species, Number of animals and Number of packages.
claims.quote: Commodity code 0102 | Common name Cow | Species Bos taurus | Number of animals 1 | Number of packages 5

claims.statement: Inside the commodity card, an 'Animal details' level-5 heading introduces a table with columns 'Animal' and 'Ear tag', one row per animal.
claims.quote: Animal details | Animal | Ear tag | Animal 1 | UK123456789012

claims.statement: The commodity card's Change link is named 'Change commodity 1' for screen readers and goes to consignment-details?change=1; the card has no anchor id, unlike every other card.
claims.quote: <A class="govuk-link" href="/live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-QQ1X0N/consignment-details?change=1">Change <SPAN class="govuk-visually-hidden"> commodity 1

claims.statement: When the transport route has transit countries, section 3 adds a 'Transit countries' subsection and card between Arrival details and Transport details; with none recorded the card is absent.
claims.ref: trace 48ae8 action call@1239; trace 8f3d8 action call@947
claims.quote: Transit countries | Countries that the consignment will travel through | France, Belgium
claims.note: The spec file says the transit-countries group waits on an overland arrival; the traces only show it present after Road Vehicle arrival with two countries added.

claims.statement: Transit countries are listed in one row, 'Countries that the consignment will travel through', as a comma-separated list.
claims.quote: France, Belgium

claims.statement: The Import details card lists rows Country of origin, Region of origin code required, Region of origin code and Internal reference number.
claims.quote: Country of origin | Region of origin code required | Region of origin code | Internal reference number

claims.statement: Country of origin reads back as the country name, and 'Region of origin code required' reads back as Yes or No.
claims.quote: Country of origin France | Region of origin code required Yes

claims.statement: The region of origin code reads back joined to the country prefix with a hyphen: suffix 'IDF75' entered for France shows as 'FR-IDF75', and '75' shows as 'FR-75'.
claims.ref: trace 17c14 actions call@813 and call@829; trace 48ae8 action call@1239
claims.quote: FR-IDF75

claims.statement: A five-character region suffix (eight characters joined) is accepted and saved.
claims.quote: Five characters after the prefix — the joined code is eight, which the old whole-code cap made impossible.

claims.statement: The internal reference the trader entered reads back as typed under 'Internal reference number'.
claims.quote: Internal reference number ReviewRef1

claims.statement: In a card that is finished, a blank optional or not-asked answer is written out as 'Not applicable' (region code when not required; internal reference left blank).
claims.quote: Region of origin code Not applicable | Internal reference number Not applicable

claims.statement: In a card that still has answers outstanding, every blank row has no visible text and carries only a visually hidden 'Missing' (class app-summary-list__value--missing), never 'Not applicable'.
claims.ref: trace 9adee actions call@1009 to call@1011; trace 11c41 actions call@667 to call@669
claims.quote: <SPAN class="app-summary-list__value--missing"><SPAN class="govuk-visually-hidden">Missing

claims.statement: Whether a blank reads 'Not applicable' or the hidden 'Missing' depends on whether its card is complete, not on whether that particular answer is required.
claims.quote: the difference is the card around it, not whether that particular answer was required

claims.statement: The Reason for import card on an unanswered notification shows one row, 'Reason for import', marked missing.
claims.quote: Reason for import [Missing]

claims.statement: The reason for import reads back by its label, for example 'Internal market', 'Transit', 'Temporary admission horses' and 'Re-entry'.
claims.ref: trace 48ae8 action call@1239; trace 8f3d8 call@947; trace d7a6d call@781; trace a28b3 call@901
claims.quote: Internal market | Transit | Temporary admission horses | Re-entry

claims.statement: For Internal market, the Reason for import card adds a 'Purpose in the market' row.
claims.quote: Purpose in the market Breeding

claims.statement: For Transit, the Reason for import card shows 'Destination country' as the country name and 'Port of exit' as port name with code, and no Exit date row.
claims.quote: Destination country Ireland | Port of exit Port of Dover (GB DVR)

claims.statement: For Temporary admission horses, the Reason for import card shows 'Exit date' and 'Port of exit', and no Destination country row.
claims.ref: trace d7a6d actions call@783 to call@787
claims.quote: Exit date 27/3/2026 | Port of exit Port of Dover (GB DVR)

claims.statement: For Re-entry, none of Destination country, Exit date or Port of exit appears on the review.
claims.ref: trace a28b3 actions call@903 to call@907
claims.quote: Reason for import Re-entry

claims.statement: Dates read back as day/month/year with no leading zeros.
claims.ref: trace d7a6d action call@783; trace 48ae8 action call@1239

claims.statement: The exit answers sit inside the Reason for import card and carry no link of their own; the card heading's Change link reaches them.
claims.quote: Change reason for import

claims.statement: The Additional animal details card shows 'Certified for' and, once answered, 'Includes unweaned animals'; unanswered it shows only 'Certified for', marked missing.
claims.ref: trace 48ae8 action call@1239; trace 11c41 action call@663
claims.quote: Certified for Slaughter | Includes unweaned animals No

claims.statement: The Arrival details card lists Port of entry, Arrival date at port of entry, Means of transport to the port of entry, Transport identification and Transport document reference.
claims.quote: Port of entry Aberdeen Harbour (GB ABD) | Arrival date at port of entry 7/11/2026 | Means of transport to the port of entry Road Vehicle | Transport identification FR-892-LK | Transport document reference CMR-2026-884721

claims.statement: On an unanswered notification, the Transport details card shows only a 'Type' row, marked missing.
claims.quote: Type [Missing]

claims.statement: Once a transporter is chosen, the Transport details card lists Name, Address (multi-line), Country, Approval number and Type.
claims.quote: Name García Livestock Transport SL | Address 43 East Hague Extension ... | Country Switzerland | Approval number ES-T2-45001294 | Type Commercial

claims.statement: The Roles and addresses card lists Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer and Place of destination.
claims.quote: Place of origin | Consignor | Consignee | Importer | Place of destination

claims.statement: Each chosen party reads back as an address block: name in bold, then address lines, postcode, country, telephone and email, each on its own line.
claims.quote: Astra Rosales / 43 East Hague Extension / Bern / 30055 / Switzerland / 01632 960000 / astra-rosales@example.com

claims.statement: Once answered, the Roles and addresses card adds a 'County parish holding (CPH) number' row showing the county, parish and holding parts run together, with no row action.

claims.quote: County parish holding (CPH) number 123456789
